headline: Sharpness 4 in 23:22 was near-textbook pacing and a club record; HRV has slid across a week with no explanation, so the Guy Fawkes block opens with a gated Saturday tempo rather than Wednesday intervals.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 4 October 2026

Shep — nothing is waiting on a reply: your 1 Oct "approve" was answered
(nothing open to approve; the plan stood). This review holds everything
already planned and extends the plan three weeks, writing the Guy Fawkes
block.

## The week

Planned: rest / 8 / 6x200 / 6 / 5 + strides / 5 / Sharpness 4. Done: all
of it, 47.1 km including the race warm-up and cool-down (the 13.1 km
entry is the whole outing). Achilles 0 every day, no first-step or
desk-chair stiffness mentioned, no hamstring mention. The 200s at RPE 2
were what they were meant to be.

## Sharpness 4: 23:22 (chip), club record

Good execution, and here is why. 3:36 for the first km when the downhill
offered 3:32, a few seconds given on the climbs, 3:41 over the high
ground, 3:11/km finish, HR building 156→176 rather than hitting a ceiling
early. That is pacing discipline you did not have at Cheltenham's start.
It was a bridge week with no real sharpening, and it is worth about
17:53 / 37:16 / 1:22:10: in line with the blended model, at or slightly
ahead. My penalties for lost sharpness and hills (10-30 s) were too
cautious by about 5 s, same direction as Cheltenham; I will use smaller
ones. One challenge: "hit lactate in the legs" at RPE 9 is fine over
4 miles, but a finish that empty is not a pattern to carry into a half or
a marathon.

## Recovery: the thing to watch

HRV 42, 38, 39, 35, 34, 35, 32 (3 Oct, UNBALANCED) against a ~40 baseline
before Cheltenham; RHR 48-49 against 46-47. Nothing in your notes explains
it (sleep 81-93, 7.7-8.9 h), so principle 3 offers no excuse: a slide
across a week outlasts any explanation. It happened in a low-load week
(ACWR 0.6-0.9), so it looks like lingering post-half cost, not this week's
running. Not a crisis, but I would not stack quality on it. Judge it on
Thursday-Friday; the race-morning number will be noisy. Spa is not the
explanation (brief, 27 Sep).

Response: week 1 has no Wednesday intervals, ~53 km, and Saturday's tempo
sits behind an HRV/RHR gate. If it has not recovered by Friday, Saturday
becomes easy running. That costs nothing: Guy Fawkes is four weeks away.

## Efficiency and form

No clean steady-run decoupling data this week (race, 200s, short easy
runs), so the read stands: aerobic base holding steady. The predictor now
blends five races: 5K 17:51, 10K 37:14, half 1:22:09, marathon 2:51:16.

## Guy Fawkes 5 (1 Nov)

Record 29:12 = 3:38/km. Riegel off Cheltenham alone gives 29:11; the
blend gives ~29:34. Sharpness came in at or ahead of the blend, so the
record looks reachable, but it still requires the block. Block: threshold
first (3x8 → 2x15 min), then 5-mile pace (5x1 km, 6x600, 2x2 miles), last
hard session 24 Oct, then a clear week. Sessions are run on pace, never
under; if RPE falls while the pace holds, that is the block working.

## Recommendation: **hold**

Nothing already planned changes. Week 1 (5-11 Oct) is firm; weeks 2-3
(12-25 Oct) are provisional. Race week gets written next Sunday.

athlete_response.thoughts: I'm in for stroud 10k on the 25/10 :)

coach_reply:
Shep — Stroud 10K on 25 Oct is logged and it was already in the plan as the October target (fixtures.json, added 4 Oct), so this changes the plan in one way only: the race week the 4 Oct proposal wrote around Guy Fawkes was never rewritten for it.

I have proposed that now: the provisional 24 Oct 2x2 miles goes (nothing hard inside ~3 days of the race), 24 Oct becomes a 30–35 min shakeout, 25 Oct is the race (~16 km with warm-up and cool-down), and Wed 21 Oct 6x600m stays as the last sharpener. Nothing heavy in the gym after that Wednesday. Weeks to 18 Oct are untouched — the threshold and 5-mile-pace work serves a 10K just as well.

Two things to carry. The projection is 37:20 (3:44/km, band 36:19–38:20) on a flat course, and Stroud is hilly, so it is a guess until we have the profile. A clubmate's file or the route would let me write real pacing next Sunday. And the HRV slide is still the gate on everything: it has to be back near baseline by race week, and Friday's reading (9 Oct) is the first checkpoint. Guy Fawkes a week later is the experiment; I'd judge it on how the legs are after Stroud, not on the record.

Approve it on the form when you're happy; it won't apply until you do.
